name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (battle/animation domain). Accurately describes the function: it animates the turn-phase banner ('ENEMY TURN'/'PLAYER TURN') sliding in, paired with fd2_animate_phase_banner_slide_out. No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: Plays the turn-phase banner slide-in animation ('ENEMY TURN' for sprite 0x52, 'PLAYER TURN' for sprite 0x50) at the start of the enemy/player turn in battle.
logic_summary: Backs up the VGA framebuffer (malloc 64000, memmove from 0xA0000). Phase 1 (slide-in, 7 frames): calls fd2_render_phase_banner_frame with x_offset = frame_iter*0x19 counting 4..0 (0x64,0x4B,0x32,0x19,0) then 1 and 0 settle frames, sliding the two banner halves from the screen edges to centre. Restores the working buffer (memmove into large_game_state_buffer) and clears the snapshot to a black frame (memset 0). Phase 2 (palette fade-in, 16 frames): for brightness 0..15 it scrolls the source block into the snapshot (fd2_scroll_buffer_block_with_wrap, scroll_offset 1..16), blits the main banner sprite (banner_sprite_id) at (0x59,0x56) and the corner frame sprite (0x51) at (0xA9,0x56), fades the VGA palette up (fd2_set_vga_palette_range 0x10..0xFF, brightness), pushes the frame to 0xA0000, and waits one BIOS tick. Finally frees the snapshot buffer and clears the keyboard buffer. The two per-frame alloc_and_blit return values are each a freshly malloc'd save buffer freed immediately after its blit (Ghidra collapsed them into one reused temp via its EAX-tracking bug; src emits two distinct frees).

params.name: param_1
params.semantics: Banner sprite chunk index: 0x50 = 'PLAYER TURN' banner, 0x52 = 'ENEMY TURN' banner. Passed to fd2_render_phase_banner_frame (slide-in) and to fd2_alloc_and_blit_indexed_sprite_chunk as the main banner sprite (fade-in).
params.reason: Live Ghidra param name is the generic placeholder param_1 (flagged needs_rename). The value is the banner sprite chunk id (0x50/0x52); src already uses banner_sprite_id. Rename to be applied in Stage 2.
